bouts.reasoning: The model has the champion at 26% against a market at 50%, which looks like age and his two knockout losses weighing heavily. Neither applies cleanly here: Evloev has never finished a UFC opponent and has little power, so the chin question matters less than against Topuria or Makhachev, and Volkanovski's takedown defence and five-round pace are built for exactly this. Evloev's chain wrestling and youth keep it small.

Yan's takedown defence beat Dvalishvili's wrestling in the rematch, and Dvalishvili has no plan B on the feet. Against that, Yan comes off lumbar disc surgery and ten months out, and a back injury is the worst thing to bring into a fight with the busiest wrestler in the sport. The model leans Dvalishvili, the market Yan; the factors cancel: no lean.
factors: Yan's takedown defence in the rematch

bouts.reasoning: Kavanagh has been knocked out by one counter (Charles Johnson) and choked when taken down (Royval); Temirov has 11 first-round finishes and knocked out Erceg in round one on his return. Temirov's year-long suspension and thin wrestling keep it small. No line or model number yet.

Volkov concedes takedowns to strong wrestlers, but Kuniev is a clinch and takedown-defence fighter more than a shooter, and his slow starts give the longer kickboxer rounds. The model is already well above the market on Volkov; no lean.

Keita has never faced a wrestler of Pico's level and took this on about five weeks' notice, two weeks after his last fight, with a weight miss in his history. Pico's chin (five early stoppage losses) against a heavy one-shot puncher keeps the lean small.
factors: Pico's wrestling vs Keita's untested defence

bouts.reasoning: Reyes has been stopped four times, twice in round one, and Murzakanov hits hard; but Murzakanov comes off his first loss, a head-kick knockout from range, and gives up reach to a long southpaw kicker. No lean.

Krylov has been stopped in three of his last four, and Yakhyaev finishes in round one; the model and market already agree at about 79%. Yakhyaev hasn't been past round one in the UFC, which is the only open question.

Rowston's wrestling defence (the DWCS loss to Finney) meets a veteran with real submissions, but Magomedov fades under sustained pressure and Rowston has won seven straight. No model number for this bout; no lean.

Dawson's three losses are all first-round knockouts, but Aliev has finished one of his last nine and is not a puncher, so Dawson's chin is less exposed than usual; Aliev's top control and youth balance Dawson's back takes in scrambles. Model and market agree; no lean.

A pressure finisher on debut against a scrappy guard player fighting outside Australia for the first time. The model and market agree near 79%; Thicknesse's triangles are the only route and Chopurov's first UFC fight the unknown.

Vagaev moves up to middleweight after tiring and nearly being submitted in round three of his debut, and has been stopped three times by strikes; Malkoun is a pressure wrestler with improved striking and three-round cardio. Malkoun's size disadvantage and injury history keep it small.
Both bring weight-cut questions (Oki's first fight at 145, Santos's botched cut at UFC 320) and both have been stopped recently. The model is already below the market on Oki; no lean.
Gugnon has one UFC fight lasting 81 seconds and has seen a third round once; Steele is a grappler who gets dragged into slugfests and withdrew from his last booking. No lean.

Lucindo's clinch strength and takedowns against a grappler who is usually out-landed on the feet; Caliari's only strawweight fight is a third-round submission. Caliari missed weight by 4.5 lb (her second career miss), which says the cut to strawweight is a struggle; she keeps the size in a catchweight bout. Lucindo's 14 months out after a doping suspension keep it small. No line or model number.
